qt: to the Commission Bert-Jan Ruissen (ECR), Geadis Geadi (ECR), Ondřej Krutílek (ECR), Mieke Andriese (PfE), Tomáš Kubín (PfE), Kristoffer Storm (ECR), Rihards Kols (ECR), Elena Donazzan (ECR), Sander Smit (PPE), Charlie Weimers (ECR), Beatrice Timgren (ECR), Dick Erixon (ECR), Fernand Kartheiser (NI), Antonio López-Istúriz White (PPE), Alexandr Vondra (ECR), Bart Groothuis (Renew), Sebastian Tynkkynen (ECR), Jorge Martín Frías (PfE), Assita Kanko (ECR) Subject:

Since the attacks of 7 October 2023, a disturbing trend has emerged: European universities and other academic institutions are increasingly severing ties with Israeli counterparts. It appears that some institutions have adopted discriminatory, antisemitic, and therefore unjustified boycotts under external pressure by activists, manifested in intimidation, vandalism, disruption and attempts to silence dissenting academics. This severely undermines academic freedom. Israeli universities and research institutions are globally recognised for their exceptional scientific contributions and technological advances. By yielding to ideological pressure from activists, European universities risk enabling antisemitism and abandoning their scientific and universal mission to advance knowledge. A petition1 has been initiated to stop EU funding for universities that terminate their cooperation with Israeli institutions and has been signed by over 3 750 people. Given that combating antisemitism and bolstering academic cooperation are European priorities: 1.
Is European universities’ adherence to the principles of non-discrimination and combating antisemitism a prerequisite for them to receive funding from the EU?
Is the Commission willing to withdraw financial support from universities that terminate existing agreements with Israeli universities? If not, what is its justification for not doing so?

(27 March 2026) The conditions to participate in and receive funding under Horizon Europe (HE) are set out in the regulation establishing HE (1) including in its Article 19(1), namely that the actions carried out must comply with ethical principles and relevant EU, national and international law, including the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights (2) and the European Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms and its Supplementary Protocols (3). Any legal entity applying for funding under HE, either on its own or as part of a consortium, must comply and continue to comply with the eligibility criteria and other call conditions for the duration of the action. Furthermore, the legal entity must declare not to be in any of the exclusion situations set out in Article 138 of the Financial Regulation (4). When becoming a beneficiary, the legal entity must respect all the obligations set out in the HE grant agreement (5). In case an exclusion situation or non-compliance is established, the responsible authorising officer has the right to take appropriate measures, which may include termination of participation. Pursuant to Article 2(2) of the Association Agreement to HE (6), Israeli entities participate in the programme under terms and conditions equivalent to those applicable to legal entities established in the EU. Accordingly, any termination of the participation of Israeli grant beneficiaries on the sole grounds of their nationality would amount to discrimination.
